name: datepicker
title: Datepicker
lead: Use Vanilla Calendar Pro through the Tremplin Datepicker adapter.

variants.title: Declarative date field
variants.description: The displayed date is locale formatted. Calendar click selection is different from manually editing the text.

variants.title: Bounded dates
variants.description: dateMin/dateMax configure the calendar; native text-input min/max do not. The sample starts in the bounded month.

variants.title: Inline calendar and explicit ISO field
variants.description: Calendar Pro replaces inline children in this pin. The copied application handler maintains a sibling hidden ISO field instead; the named region contains calendar width.

variants.title: Multiple months
variants.description: The enabled months extension shows two columns. This example explicitly sets the supported minimum-width token to 36rem so they remain side-by-side; the named region owns horizontal scrolling on mobile.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: The adapter copies the nearest cached theme ancestor to its generated calendar. RTL layout does not imply an adapter-owned keyboard policy.

variants.title: Multiple dates and range
variants.description: Multiple selection stays open; a completed range requests hide after 100 ms. Displayed separators are not a server serialization contract.

variants.title: Named button trigger
variants.description: Use a display child so the purpose text survives date updates. A button alone is not a successful submitted date field.

variants.title: Formatting, first weekday and popup theme
variants.description: This example uses an Intl format object, Sunday first and an explicit dark popup theme. This changes presentation, not ISO validation.

keyboard.behavior: Uses the adapter data API. Button toggles; inline show/hide/toggle are no-ops.

keyboard.keys: Arrow keys / Enter / Space in calendar
keyboard.behavior: Calendar Pro owns native date/month/year button focus and activation; test the generated control, not a former local-calendar API.
Requests hide through the adapter. No automatic focus restoration is promised.

guidelines: Use a labelled type=text field, not a second native type=date popup. ISO preselection is an array, while named text-input submission is formatted display text.

getSelectedDates() returns a copy. setSelectedDates() updates display but does not dispatch adapter change or native input/change. Calendar Pro replaces an inline child field; the example uses a sibling field and a disclosed click-change handler instead. Sync that field explicitly after API calls.
Manual text edits after initialization do not automatically resync the selection array. Supply an explicit application parse/validation policy or use a native date input where appropriate.

Popup visibility callbacks and promises do not establish focus restoration or async animation completion. Inline mode remains visible; disposal destroys the calendar, observer and owned outside handlers.
vcpOptions is spread before adapter-owned configuration: only the months extension is enabled, callbacks/settings can be overwritten, and sanitizer enforcement stays mandatory.
Keep the approved Calendar HTML sanitizer and same-origin dist/icons/datepicker-chevron.svg relative to dist/css. Never weaken Trusted Types/CSP to make a sample render.

The explicit contrast wrapper styles are application choices, including a Calendar Pro styles class for body-appended popups. Parent CSS inheritance alone cannot reach those popups. An explicit demo-only hidden-popup display rule prevents stale desktop coordinates from creating mobile resize overflow.

options.name: dateFormat
options.type: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions | ((date: Date, locale: string | undefined) => string) | null | undefined

events.change.trm.datepicker: Trigger notification from a calendar date click, with direct copied dates and originating event. setSelectedDates and typed text edits do not dispatch it; prevention does not undo selection.
events.click.trm.datepicker: Internal namespaced trigger listener, not a dispatched Datepicker lifecycle event.
events.focusin.trm.datepicker: Internal namespaced outside-focus listener, not a dispatched Datepicker lifecycle event.
events.hidden.trm.datepicker: Trigger notification after Calendar Pro hide() is called, not a guaranteed delayed animation completion or focus-return event.
events.hide.trm.datepicker: Cancelable trigger event before adapter hide(); inline mode does not hide. Outside focus/pointer paths also request adapter hide.
events.pointerdown.trm.datepicker: Internal namespaced outside-pointer listener, not a dispatched Datepicker lifecycle event.
events.show.trm.datepicker: Cancelable trigger event before adapter show(); disabled/already-open and inline cases return without it.
events.shown.trm.datepicker: Trigger notification immediately after Calendar Pro show() is called; no focus-restoration or transition-completion promise is supplied.

sourceOptions.name: datepickerTheme
sourceOptions.description: Explicit popup theme overrides the cached nearest theme ancestor; auto maps to Calendar Pro system.

sourceOptions.name: dateMin
sourceOptions.description: Forwarded date bound; use a supported date such as YYYY-MM-DD, not text-input min.

sourceOptions.name: dateMax
sourceOptions.description: Forwarded maximum date; not a server scheduling/validation policy.

sourceOptions.name: dateFormat
sourceOptions.description: Formatting object/function for display. Default is locale date formatting, not ISO submission.

sourceOptions.name: displayElement
sourceOptions.description: Separate display; non-input triggers prefer a data-trm-datepicker-display child. false suppresses extra display, not input updates.

sourceOptions.name: displayMonthsCount
sourceOptions.description: Supported months extension; more than one selects multiple calendar layout.

sourceOptions.name: firstWeekday
sourceOptions.description: Monday by default; 0 is Sunday.

sourceOptions.name: inline
sourceOptions.description: Always-visible inline mode; show/hide/toggle are no-ops. Calendar Pro replaces children in this pin; the shown application handler maintains a separate sibling hidden field instead.

sourceOptions.name: locale
sourceOptions.description: Calendar locale and display formatting locale; default uses the environment.

sourceOptions.name: positionElement
sourceOptions.description: Position relative to this element, otherwise an input form-adorn ancestor or the trigger.

sourceOptions.name: selectedDates
sourceOptions.description: Initial selected date array; dates also choose the opening month/year.

sourceOptions.name: selectionMode
sourceOptions.description: single, multiple or multiple-ranged. Single/nonempty and completed ranged clicks request hide after 100 ms.

sourceOptions.name: placement
sourceOptions.description: Calendar Pro left/center/right/auto placement, not Floating UI placements.

sourceOptions.name: vcpOptions
sourceOptions.description: Spread first, then adapter-owned callbacks, sanitizer and months extension/config overwrite collisions. Other extension-only features are not enabled.

name: otp-input
title: Otp Input
description: Otp Input component documentation for Tremplin.
lead: Collect one-time codes in one native input with decorative visual slots.

variants.title: Verification code
variants.description: One named real input backs all slots; no code is transmitted by this page.

variants.title: Six-digit code
variants.description: The six-slot example explicitly uses responsive size/gap tokens; copy them with the markup. Core defaults remain unchanged.

variants.title: Masked display
variants.description: Masking affects visual dots only. The real type=text input, accessible value and FormData still contain the synthetic sample code.

variants.title: Invalid code
variants.description: The authored description/aria-invalid mark an application error, not a result from complete events.
variants.markup: Request a new code.

variants.title: Connected and grouped letters
variants.description: Actual connected slots and decorative groups. ASCII filters keep one value; group separators do not become submitted characters.

variants.title: Native sizes
variants.description: Use otp-sm/lg on the wrapper. These are still one field each, not independent per-slot inputs.

variants.title: Readonly and disabled
variants.description: Native attributes block user edits. Programmatic setValue/clear are not gated by readonly/disabled; disposal does not restore all mutated input attributes.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Slots follow direction visually. The pinned pointer hit-test still scans physical right edges in DOM order; do not claim complete RTL tapping support.

keyboard.behavior: Uses one real input with overwrite/deletion interception, not independent digit fields.
Native caret/selection drives one decorative active slot. Keyboard focus targets the first empty or last full slot.
ASCII sanitize before truncating. A full sanitized paste replaces the whole value; shorter pastes use the selection.

guidelines: Put data-trm-otp on a wrapper with one labelled named input. Slots/separators are generated and aria-hidden; no slot-by-slot ARIA or custom arrow roving contract is supplied.
Runtime event suffix is .trm.otpInput. The frozen scanner uses the filename otp-input; these pages correct presentation only, not core or baseline metadata.
setValue() sanitizes and can emit complete repeatedly, but not plugin input. clear() clears and focuses without plugin input/complete. User changes emit plugin input then completion checks.
Masking is visual only; no hashing, server verification, transport, expiry or attempt-limit policy is supplied. Do not log codes or automatically submit on a completion notification.

Readonly/disabled guard user handlers, not programmatic value methods. dispose removes generated slots/listeners/rendered class, but does not restore type, maxlength, inputmode, pattern or otp-input class.
The RTL pointer algorithm is not direction-aware. Confirm real-device tap positions, SMS/password-manager autofill and assistive technology behavior separately from automated desktop checks.

events.complete.trm.otpInput: Wrapper notification each time the completion check sees a full value, including repeated setValue calls. value is direct and sensitive; never log it. Not a validation result or cancellation gate.
events.input.trm.otpInput: Wrapper notification after a user input/paste/overwrite/delete path, with direct value. setValue and clear do not emit this plugin notification; a bubbling native input is a separate event.

sourceOptions.name: groups
sourceOptions.description: Decorative group lengths. The final configured size repeats for remaining groups; separators never enter the input value.

sourceOptions.name: length
sourceOptions.description: Truthy configured length, otherwise valid maxlength or six. Use a positive sensible length; no integer/range validation is supplied.

sourceOptions.name: mask
sourceOptions.description: Dots replace only decorative slot text. The real input stays text and still submits the value.

sourceOptions.name: separator
sourceOptions.description: Plain text between configured groups, not HTML.

sourceOptions.name: type
sourceOptions.description: numeric, alpha or alphanumeric use ASCII filters and matching inputmode/pattern; unknown strings fall back to numeric.

name: range
title: Range
lead: Enhance a native slider inside a form-range wrapper with fill, bubble and datalist ticks.

variants.title: Value bubble
variants.description: Range belongs to the wrapper. A bare bubble attribute enables the generated decorative output.

variants.title: Datalist ticks
variants.description: Option labels are literal text. The pin sorts/clamps numeric positions; formatter does not format these labels.

variants.title: Disabled slider
variants.description: Native disabled prevents user focus/edits; the API can still recompute a programmatic value.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Native keyboard behavior follows the browser, but pinned gradient and bubble use physical left/to-right coordinates. No RTL correction is applied to core.

variants.title: Bounds, fractional steps and no bubble
variants.description: Actual native constraints and a wrapper without a bubble; the fill still needs Range JavaScript.

variants.title: Theme colors
variants.description: A supported theme class on the token-owning wrapper colors the fill and thumb.

variants.title: Custom bubble formatter
variants.description: The copied browser-bundle setup deliberately replaces any auto-created instance before configuring a percent bubble. It does not change native value/submission or tick labels.

variants.title: Programmatic update and native submission
variants.description: This explicit application button sets the native value and calls update(); it does not submit or synthesize input/change.
variants.markup: Demo value is 40. This page does not submit data.

keyboard.behavior: Native range keyboard rules and min/max/step constraints remain browser-owned. A bubble is not an interactive Tooltip plugin.

guidelines: Use form-range around one labelled form-range-input; every matching wrapper auto-initializes on document ready.
The wrapper receives --trm-range-fill as a ratio, not a percentage. Native bounds supply 0/100 when absent; min>=max makes the adapter ratio zero.
After assigning input.value, call update(). Construction/update and native input/change paths emit changed on the actual input, even when unchanged; it is not a cancelable mutation gate.
Formatter text uses textContent for the bubble only. Tick labels read option.label without formatter; datalist points are snapshotted once, sorted and clamped to positions.
The bubble and ticks are aria-hidden. Native name/value submit the numeric value; formatter does not create aria-valuetext or convert submitted units.

Pinned track gradient is to right and bubble uses left even in RTL; test native thumb versus decoration rather than claiming direction-aware fill. dispose removes generated bubble/ticks/listeners but retains the wrapper fill property.

events.changed.trm.range: Notification on the native input after construction, update(), input or change, even if the numeric value is unchanged. Direct value is numeric; canceling does not roll back the slider.

sourceOptions.name: bubble
sourceOptions.description: Show a tooltip-shaped decorative output. A bare data-trm-bubble normalizes to enabled.

sourceOptions.name: formatter
sourceOptions.description: Formats bubble text with textContent. In this pin tick labels use datalist option.label directly; they are not passed through formatter.

name: strength
title: Strength
lead: Provide advisory segmented password feedback with a readable text message.

variants.title: Segmented feedback
variants.description: Synthetic prefilled text is evaluated on initialization. This score is illustrative feedback, not evidence that a real password is safe.

variants.title: Empty password
variants.description: Default zero score yields no level. Text/segment updates happen on transitions; do not pre-author misleading feedback in an initially empty meter.

variants.title: Single bar
variants.description: The actual strength-bar CSS derives width from the level attribute. The native password field remains the only editable input.

variants.title: Custom local scorer
variants.description: The copied demo function uses length only and complete message keys. This is a deliberately simple illustration, not a security recommendation.

variants.title: Static CSS states
variants.description: Each bar has authored state and readable context, without a linked password input or an ARIA numeric-meter promise.
variants.markup:
weak

fair

good

strong

variants.title: Native readonly and disabled inputs
variants.description: Native input states control user editing; evaluate() still reads an application-assigned value. Nothing is submitted by this page.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: Text status and segment count accompany color; these bars never receive focus.

keyboard.behavior: Input/change evaluations follow the real password field. Decorative bars/segments never enter the tab sequence.

guidelines: Use explicit data-trm-input or a single password field per parent; the text feedback is the first strength-text in the meter parent, not an arbitrary global target.
Default scoring uses eight length/category points. Zero maps to null; thresholds [2,4,6] are inclusive ceilings. This heuristic is not authentication policy or a compromised-password check.
strengthChange is dispatched only when the level changes. Different scores within the same level do not refresh text or dispatch a new plugin event. Event password is redacted as *** or empty.

Nested messages/weights replace their default objects rather than deep-merging. Supply all keys; missing weight keys can yield NaN and an accidental strong result. Validate custom scorer outputs and thresholds separately.
A custom scorer is called only for nonempty text. minLength affects scoring, not native minlength or form validity. evaluate() is needed after programmatic value changes.

There is no numeric ARIA meter. Decorative aria-hidden segments/bar and an associated readable polite status are application markup; dispose removes owned input listeners but leaves the displayed DOM/state.

events.strengthChange.trm.strength: Wrapper notification only when the level changes, including nonempty initial evaluation. Direct strength/score and redacted password (*** or empty) are supplied. Not every score change, and not a mutation veto.

sourceOptions.name: input
sourceOptions.description: Selector/element, otherwise the first password input in the parent. Give separate meters separate parents or explicit input selectors.

sourceOptions.name: minLength
sourceOptions.description: Adds a length scoring point; does not enforce input minlength or reject a password.

sourceOptions.name: messages
sourceOptions.defaultValue: { weak: Weak, fair: Fair, good: Good, strong: Strong }
sourceOptions.description: Complete per-level text map. Nested option objects replace defaults rather than merging individual keys.

sourceOptions.name: weights
sourceOptions.defaultValue: { minLength:1, extraLength:1, lowercase:1, uppercase:1, numbers:1, special:1, multipleSpecial:1, longPassword:1 }
sourceOptions.description: Supply every key. A partial replacement can add undefined values and produce NaN; custom scoring bypasses this map.

sourceOptions.name: thresholds
sourceOptions.description: Inclusive weak/fair/good ceilings; above the third is strong, zero returns null. No length/order validation is supplied.

sourceOptions.name: scorer
sourceOptions.description: Local custom function for nonempty text; empty text returns zero before calling it. Validate custom return values in your application.
